title.justification: The paper's title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document.

analysis.description: This paper introduces the concept of affordances for options in reinforcement learning and develops temporally abstract partial option models to improve the efficiency of planning and learning. The paper analyzes the trade-offs between estimation and approximation error when using such models and demonstrates their empirical impact on planning efficiency, particularly in the Taxi domain.

type.justification: The study is primarily theoretical as it introduces new frameworks and provides theoretical analysis regarding the use and impact of temporally abstract partial option models in reinforcement learning. Though empirical analysis is mentioned, the primary focus is on theoretical underpinnings and proofs.
type.quote: In this paper, we define a notion of affordances for options, and develop temporally abstract partial option models, that take into account the fact that an option might be affordable only in certain situations. We analyze the trade-offs between estimation and approximation error in planning and learning when using such models, and identify some interesting special cases.

name.justification: The research falls under the domain of reinforcement learning, as it focuses on option models, a concept used within reinforcement learning to allow temporal abstractions.
name.quote: We work in the context of model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) and temporal abstraction in the framework of options Sutton et al. (1999).

name.justification: The paper specifically deals with model-based reinforcement learning as it discusses the creation of models to help in planning and decision-making processes.
name.quote: We work in the context of model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) and temporal abstraction in the framework of options Sutton et al. (1999).

name.justification: Option Models are the primary deep learning model discussed and extended in the paper.
name.quote: Options define a way of behaving, including a set of states in which an option can start, an internal policy that is used to make decisions while the option is executing, and a stochastic, state-dependent termination condition.

is_contributed.justification: The paper proposes enhancements to the existing option model framework by incorporating the notion of affordances and partial models, thus contributing to the field.
is_contributed.quote: In this paper, we define a notion of affordances for options, and develop temporally abstract partial option models.

is_executed.justification: There is no indication that the models were actually executed or implemented; the focus is on theoretical development.
is_executed.quote: The paper focuses on developing models and their theoretical underpinnings rather than executing them.

is_compared.justification: The paper develops theoretical models and does not compare their performance numerically with other models.
is_compared.quote: The focus of the paper is on developing theoretical models and frameworks, and their practical implications are discussed in principle, rather than through numerical comparison with extant models.

referenced_paper_title.value: Between mdps and semi-mdps: A framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning
referenced_paper_title.justification: The foundational option model was initially proposed in the referenced paper by Sutton et al., and the current paper builds upon that framework.
referenced_paper_title.quote: In reinforcement learning, option models (Sutton, Precup & Singh, 1999; Precup, 2000) provide the framework for this kind of temporally abstract prediction and reasoning.
